PullRequest.Title: notifications: unify toast spacing
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #334182

## Problem

Modern UI notification toasts had an 8px gutter at the right edge, but only a 4px gutter above the 28px status rail. Stacked toasts also combined adjacent 4px margins, producing an 8px internal gap. This made the toast placement and stack rhythm look inconsistent.

## Fix

- Changed the default bottom inset to the existing `--vscode-spacing-size360` token: 28px status rail + 8px outer gutter.
- Preserved the existing 8px inline gutter.
- Removed the bottom margin from every non-final toast so stacked surfaces use one 4px gap instead of two combined margins.
- Added regression coverage for the default inset and first-versus-last toast margins.

## Result

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---:|
| Right outer gutter | 8px |
| Bottom outer gutter above status rail | 8px |
| Status rail height | 28px |
| Total bottom inset | 36px |
| Gap between stacked toast surfaces | 4px |

The scenarios use notifications created through the real VS Code extension API, including severity icons, source labels, actions, stacking, shadows, and status-bar positioning.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show, stack, and dismiss Modern UI notification toasts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A notification model ADD is queued to the next animation frame, creates/inserts a toast, updates its list, measures toast heights, and lays out the bounded stack before display. The changed :not(:last-child) rule participates in normal style resolution during that existing DOM/layout path but adds no separate synchronous read or extra pass.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible toast siblings after height filtering, capped at 3; hidden toasts are removed from the toast container DOM and do not participate in the structural selector.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pending toast additions are scheduled at the next animation frame; spam protection permits at most 3 additions per 800 ms, and layout displays at most 3 toast DOM nodes. Add/remove mutations are handled synchronously on the UI thread without subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or memoized boundary is involved. The notifications container is lazily created once; selector matching and layout use the current bounded DOM on each add/remove.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that sibling insertion/removal can invalidate :last-child matching, and high confidence from NotificationsToasts.MAX_NOTIFICATIONS plus DOM removal that the affected set is bounded to three.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific selector invalidation cost is not measured, but cardinality is statically capped at three and the path already measures and lays out every toast, so the added matching cannot establish a meaningful regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff changes one margin declaration for non-final visible toasts; any extra selector matching is constant-bounded and does not introduce an additional layout boundary or realistically user-visible rendering cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display or reposition the Modern UI notification center and toast container across status-bar and configured notification positions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS style resolution computes the notification center/toast top, bottom, left, and right offsets when the elements are shown or their position classes change. The diff substitutes an existing spacing custom property value and does not add JS work, geometry reads, or another relayout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One notification center container and one toast container per workbench window; auxiliary windows independently apply the same stylesheet.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread style/layout update per relevant DOM/class/configuration change; no queue fan-out or asynchronous external operations are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CSS is bundled at startup and remains inert until the Modern UI class is present. Custom-property resolution follows normal browser style caching; no application cache keys, misses, coalescing, or negative caching are involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the CSS diff and owning contribution that only computed inset values change on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style recalculation duration varies by browser and workbench DOM size, but the changed declarations preserve selector count and property count for these offsets.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: changing size320 to size360 alters geometry only and introduces no additional CPU, layout, I/O, memory, or concurrency mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the isolated Modern UI notification/dialog presentation regression test
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The synchronous browser unit test creates one additional toast container, requests one additional computed style, and compares two margin values. This is test-only work and runs once per test invocation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant: one additional DOM container/toast and one getComputedStyle call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous within one test; no external boundaries or parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior is changed; styles are read from the test document once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed test hunk.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material uncertainty: the added work is constant and test-only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the constant one-element/one-style-read increase cannot affect product performance or materially affect test-suite throughput.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced notification creation, DOM visibility, layout, positioning, and test execution. The only new selector-sensitive work is bounded to at most three visible toast siblings; all offset changes are value substitutions. No expensive boundary, unbounded retention, repeated scaling work, concurrency burst, or actionable performance regression was introduced.
